title: Crispy-Skin Chicken Alfredo
summary: Fettuccine in a garlic, thyme and two-cheese cream sauce, topped with boneless chicken thighs seared skin-side down until crisp and finished in the oven.
notes: The video states only the garlic (4 cloves), the Parmigiano (about 1/2 cup) and the pasta (1 lb, store-bought). Everything else is our estimate for a 1 lb batch: 4 thighs, 1 tbsp oil, 2 cups cream, 2 tbsp butter, 1/2 cup pecorino, seasonings. Servings (4) follow from 1 lb pasta and 4 thighs. 'About a half cup grated' may describe the Parmigiano or the pecorino; we read it as the Parmigiano and gave the pecorino the same. He also makes a fresh pasta dough from his cookbook; that is a side demonstration and is left out. Oven temperature is not said; 400 F is ours. The video says the recipe is on his website: compare against it before approving.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, covered so it heats faster, and salt it generously.
Debone the thighs: cut down the underside along the bone, work your fingers and the knife tip around it, and scrape it free. Keep the skin on. Save the bones for stock if you like.
Pat the skin very dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Lay the thighs in skin side down and press them flat for the first minute so they don't curl. Cook until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip the thighs, turn off the burner, and move the skillet to the oven. Roast until the thickest part reads 165°F, then rest the chicken.
While the chicken roasts, finely grate both cheeses. Use a block, not pre-grated cheese: anti-caking starch makes the sauce grainy.
In a wide sauté pan over medium heat, add the cream and butter. Stir in the garlic, thyme and pepper, and let it simmer and reduce. A wider pan reduces faster.
Cook the fettuccine in the boiling water until just al dente.
Raise the heat under the sauce and whisk in about half the cheese until smooth, then the rest. Grate in the nutmeg.
Lift the pasta straight into the sauce with tongs so some cooking water comes with it. Toss until glossy, adding a splash more pasta water if it's thick. Taste and adjust the salt.
Slice the chicken and serve it over the pasta, with extra Parmigiano on top.
